newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips close mixed, SAX slips 0.55.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips close mixed, SAX slips 0.55.

text.p: Major Slovak stocks were mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, but losses to several blue chips pulled the SAX index down 0.55 points to 194.8.

Slovakia's largest commercial bak VUB was the biggest net loser on the session, down 60 crowns to 1,700. Brokers said that with just two shares traded, VUB appeared to be only being tasted by potential investors.
Oil refiner Slovnaft, the heaviest issue on the BSE floor, lost 10 crowns to 855. Dealers said the issue, like most blue chips, seemed undervalued for larger packages.
"We think that most of the blue chips are still undervalued and we expect their growth potential to keep the market on upward trend in the mid-term," said Radovan Dzugas of Creditanstalt.
He said drug producer Slovakofarma continued to be the fastest rising share on the unlisted market, climbing another 65 crowns to 4,565 on Thursday.
"The demand for Slovakofarma remains strong, giving the share the potential to rise even to around 4,650 crowns," Dzugas said.

Steel producer VSZ led activity with 17,736 shares changing hands, but closed unchanged at 685 crowns. Brokers said the volume was one package traded twice through the market floor and that they considered the current issue's price as a real market value.
Overall volume fell to 365,153 shares, from 443,974 stocks traded on Wednesday. Turnover declining to 177.34 million crowns, from 737.53 million.
